sections.content: Writers and speakers use a few devices to make a point stick. Three are easy to spot and easy to use.

sections.title: Three devices
sections.content: A metaphor says that one thing *is* another, without *como*: *El tiempo es un río* does not mean time has water; it means time flows and does not come back. With *como* it is a comparison, not a metaphor: *El tiempo pasa como un río*. A rhetorical question is asked to make a point, not to get an answer: *¿Quién puede negar que los precios suben?* means "nobody can deny it". Repetition puts the same word in a row to stress an idea: *Trabajo, trabajo y más trabajo: así se aprende.*

items.spanish: ¿Quién puede negar que los precios suben?
items.english: Who can deny that prices are rising? (rhetorical question)

items.spanish: Trabajo, trabajo y más trabajo: así se aprende.
items.english: Work, work and more work: that is how one learns. (repetition)

sections.content: Use one device at a time. A metaphor works best if you keep it going for a sentence or two (*El tiempo es un río: corre, no vuelve*), and a rhetorical question is strongest at the end of a paragraph. If a plain sentence says it better, keep the plain sentence.
